Header:

Artifacts referenced: partner_intro_deck.pdf (shared), nvlink-benchmark-template.xlsx (link), redwood-security-one-pager.pdf
Attendees: Sophie Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Amira Patel (QB CTO), Liam O'Connor (QB Head Infra), Sara N'Komo (QB VP Partnerships)

Summary (auto): quick partner intro, high-level arch discussion around GPU topologies + commercial model, agree to bench plan + next technical deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Kim: Hey everyone, Sophie from Redwood, thanks for making time. Quick round robin?
[00:06] Amira Patel: Amira here - CTO at QuantumBridge Orbit, hi all.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Liam, infra, running the GPU park.
[00:10] Sara N'Komo: Sara, partnerships.
[00:12] Diego Martinez: Diego, infra SE on Redwood side.
[00:15] Sophie Kim: Cool, super. Goal for today is intro, surface any blockers for an integration and outline a small poc / benchmark. We'll be pretty practical.
[00:26] Amira Patel: Sounds good. For context, we're a satellite imagery analytics SaaS and we do large ensemble inference for rectification and object detection, increasing LLM use for prompts and post-processing. Currently using internal inference stack plus a cloud partner for bursts.
[00:42] Liam O'Connor: Fleet is mostly A100s, some H100 pre-orders, mix of NVLink and PCIe-only nodes. We're exploring MIG-like partitioning and MPS to multiplex workloads.
[00:55] Sophie Kim: Great. Quick question on tenancy — you're looking at a channel partner integration (we route customers through you) or co-sale where Redwood would route some capacity into your infra?
[01:08] Sara N'Komo: We want to surface QuantumBridge as a certified hardware partner for customers who need on-prem or colocation with low-lat. Also exploring dedicated pools where we host redwood runtime on your gear for enterprise customers.
[01:23] Diego Martinez: Okay that maps to two paths: 1) partner distribution + integration (we validate models on your infra, we label it as 'QuantumBridge verified') and 2) private/dedicated deployment where customer can buy Redwood Dedicated but the GPUs live with you. Both are doable but have different ops and legal needs.
[01:40] Amira Patel: Ops wise we care about control plane. We prefer customer-managed VPC w/ private control plane, not hosted multitenant. SOC2 and SAML SSO are musts. How does Redwood handle that?
[01:53] Sophie Kim: Redwood Private supports a customer-controlled control plane, and we integrate with SAML/SSO and KMS/HSM for key management. We have an enterprise page on gov/compliance but I'll share the SOC2 report.
[02:03] Liam O'Connor: Quick nit: how heavy is the telemetry? We need to know what logs leave the environment — audit logs, token-level cost stats?
[02:12] Diego Martinez: We can ship usage/metrics in a configurable way. For private deployments you can opt-in to telemetry, and token-level anonymized usage can be sent to Redwood Console for billing. For air-gapped we support offline log bundles and local metrics collection. (slight static)
[02:30] Amira Patel: Nice. On the bench front — we want to understand throughput for short-context chat style workloads vs long sequence generation for embedds and full-frame processing. Also curious about latency SLOs if you route through a partner host.
[02:44] Sophie Kim: For partner-hosted infra we typically measure p50/p95 latency and throughput per-GPU and report tokens/sec. Our Optimize tooling recommends batching/kv-caching to hit cost targets. For your mixed NVLink/PCIe nodes, kernel selection matters a lot — we can bias to H100-optimized kernels for very large context.
[03:05] Liam O'Connor: Are there special drivers? We run a custom kernel set and occasionally have to lock CUDA versions — compatibility is commonly a blocker.
[03:14] Diego Martinez: We support a matrix of CUDA + cuDNN versions; the runtime has fallbacks but yes, matching kernels ideally. For private deployments we can work with your ops team to build pinned images.
[03:27] Amira Patel: Licensing / revenue share question: if we surface Redwood as a partner and host dedicated pools, how do commercials look? Flat fee? Rev share? Is there a channel program?
[03:40] Sophie Kim: We have a partner program with tiers. For hosters: revenue share on committed pools + minimum monthly for support. For channel-only referrals we do finder fees and co-marketing. I'll send a redlineable commercial framework.
[03:54] Sara N'Komo: Great, please include any lead-gen co-marketing templates.
[03:58] Diego Martinez: Technical thought — for telemetry and routing policy, can we map by policy (latency-first, cost-first, region)?
[04:07] Sophie Kim: Yes, smart routing exists. Policies can be set per-customer or per-route; fallback model variants are automatic when cap constrained. Important note: model variants must be validated for quality differences; Optimize can help us flag regressions.
[04:21] Amira Patel: On the model side, we run some proprietary LLMs (4B/8B) and open LLaMA variants. Will Redwood handle quantized checkpoints?
[04:30] Diego Martinez: Yes, runtime supports int8 and 4-bit per model families; we also have kernel paths optimized for quantized ops. We'll want to know your typical sequence lengths to pick kernels.
[04:41] Liam O'Connor: Bandwidth question: when using NVLink across multi-GPU nodes for KV cache sharing, do you use any custom sync or rely on NCCL?
[04:51] Diego Martinez: We leverage NCCL + our KV cache sharding logic. There are tradeoffs for multi-GPU sharded KV vs single-GPU large memory. We'll test both patterns in the bench.
[05:03] Amira Patel: Can you run a short micro-benchmark on our nodes? We can give a dev node with one H100 NVLink pair and one PCIe node.
[05:11] Sophie Kim: Absolutely — we propose: small bench (chat 2k tokens with 8B model), embed bench (batch embeddings 512), and a longgen pass (16k tokens) to see mem/cost. Diego to draft plan.
[05:24] Sara N'Komo: On security — we'll need SOC2, SAML, RBAC, tenant isolation, and clear data residency. Also legal needs the data flow diagram.
[05:35] Sophie Kim: Noted, will send SOC2 and dataflow diagram, and an example DPA.
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: One operational ask: if we host dedicated pools, do you expect us to run the orchestrator? Are there ops agents?
[05:49] Diego Martinez: For partner-hosted dedicated, there's a small agent and a runtime image. We provide an operator to run on k8s or on baremetal systemd. We also offer managed ops as an add-on.
[06:01] Amira Patel: Are there minimum commit sizes for dedicated pools? We need to present to finance.
[06:07] Sophie Kim: Yes, depends on region and SLAs; I'll include a few pricing bands in the commercial framework.
[06:12] Liam O'Connor: Bandwidth/cost - we also want metrics we can expose to customers via our portal (detailed billing). Is that possible?
[06:20] Diego Martinez: Yes, for dedicated/private we can export per-customer billing metrics as CSV or a push to your billing endpoint.
[06:28] Amira Patel: Any blockers you've seen with other GPU partners?
[06:32] Diego Martinez: Typical blockers: mismatched CUDA versions, security approvals around KMS, and expectations around telemetry. Also sometimes customers expect immediate model drop-in compatibility which requires quantization/compilation step.
[06:46] Sophie Kim: Maybe call out a quick risk: model quality regression when switching kernels or quant. We have Optimize/Evals to detect that early.
[06:55] Amira Patel: Good to know. For the poc timeline — we want results by mid-Jan to present at a board meeting. Is that realistic?
[07:03] Sophie Kim: Yes, if we start early December. Diego: are we aligned to do the micro-bench this week and schedule deep-dive in week of Dec 15?
[07:11] Diego Martinez: Yes, I'll draft the bench and availability.
[07:15] Sara N'Komo: I'll coordinate legal/partner ops side.
[07:18] Sophie Kim: Cool, let's recap next steps.
